study.question: Does removing the need for a fixed auxiliary projection to fit the low click-rate offset recover history usefulness, or does its dispersion constraint itself harm the frozen predictor?
study.hypothesis: Local observations: feature-only AUC=0.6050036145, pooled=0.6102261137, DIN-style=0.6133619861. Aligned history auxiliary BCE lost 0.0004605540, while expected-permuted learned-head loss gained 0.0002716801; target-only and permuted controls prevent attributing gains to aligned history supervision. Learned M-only=0.6133191315 and D-only=0.6135891495 do not establish additive effects. Fixed-shape full loss fell to 0.6078643414; blocked variants reproduced baseline exactly. On the candidate-supplied first-512-row diagnostic, fixed routed pooled norm=11.90457 versus blocked=5.80831, entropy=2.28285 versus 3.29882. Learned Jacobian norm=0.01644 versus initial-shape Jacobian=0.20517 on the same final pool; fixed Jacobian=0.18758. This is consistent with, but does not prove, adaptive attenuation of a calibration burden. A fixed output bias may adapt too slowly, making encoder shifts fit prevalence. Centering should remove that route while retaining a dispersion signal. Alternative: sustained projection gradients themselves cause harm. No training time series is supplied, so the slow-bias account remains unobserved.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit target-aware field-adapted attention, not exact DIN: local attention is normalized while the source explicitly removes softmax. Source minibatch-aware L2 penalizes sparse embeddings with frequency correction. Proposed loss instead centers a scalar training-only history projection and uses current training-label prevalence; no claim it reproduces source regularization.

Verified only author field warning: histories have category, brand and behavior type but no item. Full publisher method remains unavailable; no item-level matching, future behavior or DMR mechanism reproduction is claimed.

nearest_work.source_ref: g3-r0001-expected_permuted; g3-r0002-fixed_routed; g3-r0002-learned_routed; ancestor sources inspected
nearest_work.difference: Inherit primary backbone, RNG isolation, auxiliary head, expected-label decomposition and no-grad diagnostics. New loss subtracts the differentiable batch mean of projection logits and imposes an analytic prevalence offset; fixed M/D ablations locate the native loss failure. This follows negative transfer, not an external architecture prescription. Broader novelty unverified: authorized searches for confidence/label smoothing, auxiliary calibration and centering/intercept returned no additional primary sources; lack of search hits is not priority evidence.

inherited_components: All frozen host causal features, exposure labels, scorers, temporal splits, history truncation and training/checkpoint rules. Raw tables, data constructors and training internals are not public inputs here; use inherited frozen receipts rather than pretend to re-audit them.
Reference category/brand/action/recency embeddings, normalized target-aware pool and static+history MLP; exact construction order and same default Adam learning rate.
Expected-label M/D algebra and 577-parameter head allocated under torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]); initial-head snapshots for descriptive diagnostics.

Learned and fixed blocked controls reproduce baseline; these are sanity checks at the same seed, not independent repetitions. No failed execution is recorded; negative executed branches and omitted independent repetitions remain visible.
study.proposed_difference: Add a training-only shift-invariant centered Jensen-gap loss C; keep mean(z) in the graph so valid-logit gradients sum to zero. Use only supplied current-training labels for detached q; clamp q at 1e-4 and 1-1e-4, omit the redundant final head bias from this branch, and zero auxiliary contributions for batches without valid history. Cross with fixed/learned head shape and complete native fixed M/D contrasts using existing full and blocked anchors. Neither pooled features nor logits are centered at inference. No optimizer, data-pass, capacity or prediction change is added. Candidate diagnostics are label-free and include raw-head variance/Jacobian, history covariance, mean-vector norm and centered gap at zero; raw auxiliary probabilities do not describe centered training calibration. Preparation checks completed: study structural-schema validation (jsonschema package unavailable), Python syntax compilation in memory, allowed-import/no-I/O source audit, exact AST equality of _encode and forward with ancestor, matching literal/registered configs, and 25 finite-form scalar diagnostics within the 64-key interface. Independent scalar finite differences confirmed the centered gradient identity, zero sum, common-shift invariance, invalid-row masking, empty/singleton-history behavior and clipped q=0/1 boundaries. These do not verify Torch execution, numerical model logits, GPU cost or quality; all host execution remains pending.
predictions: Algebraic prediction, not a performance finding: C is invariant to a common auxiliary-logit shift; masked valid-logit gradient is (sigmoid(c+z_i-m)-mean_valid sigmoid(c+z-m))/n and sums to zero. Empty-history and single-valid-history batches have zero auxiliary gradient.

Calibration-burden hypothesis predicts fixed M-only will reproduce a substantial fraction of the full fixed loss, whereas fixed D-only will recover toward baseline. This contrast is allowed to falsify the explanation.

Predeclared screen: centered_fixed recovers >=0.002 AUC over g3-r0002-fixed_routed and has lower diagnostic pooled norm than 11.90457. This is recovery, not evidence of beating baseline. Centering should help fixed more than learned if head adaptability was compensating for mean calibration.

Inspect the frozen existing history-length slices (0,1-16,17-64,>64), behavior presence, time, frequency and category-match slices with sample/positive/negative counts. Prior fixed losses were -0.01277015, -0.00729056, -0.00550638 AUC in the three nonempty length bins; empty-history improved 0.00325943, so shared embeddings/global training can affect empty histories. Treat slice findings as exploratory; no post-hoc confirmatory claim.
falsifiers: If centered fixed fails the recovery/norm predictions and fixed D-only is also poor, a mean-calibration-only explanation is inadequate.
If M-only is near baseline but D-only resembles full fixed, dispersion constraints are a better local lead than a mean calibration burden.

If centering helps fixed and learned equally, weaken a fixed-head-specific compensation account. If learned-head gain disappears across paired seeds, do not claim improvement from the native auxiliary signal.

Finite, shift-invariant loss and zero-sum gradients are implementation properties, not evidence that the representation is more predictive. If AUC/logloss do not improve against closest references, retain the simpler/better supported predictor.
Any invalid logits, runtime error, field access outside the batch, package/network/filesystem access from model code, or frozen-contract mismatch invalidates the arm; its consumed costs stay charged.
alternative_explanations: Auxiliary weight 0.2 produces different gradient norms under different centering/curvature and head adaptation; no effective-strength matching or equal-compute frontier has been measured.
Fixed random head constraints may suppress useful click directions or induce ReLU-region escape. One scalar projection does not characterize full representation quality.
Head/encoder coadaptation, static/history shared embeddings, low event identity resolution, natural imbalance and checkpoint timing could explain outcomes.
Small incumbent gain may be seed variation or validation search selection; first-512-row norm and covariance are descriptive biased-prefix measurements.
Static publisher snapshot as-of dates remain undocumented, and source pCVR/delay tasks differ from this CTR task. No unseen item IDs, delay targets, test outcomes or personal knowledge are assumed.

contrasts.intervention: fixed_mean_only: fixed head M=1,D=0; fixed_dispersion_only: fixed head M=0,D=1, both retaining the native trainable final bias.
contrasts.control: Complete the fixed-head M x D factorial using existing g3-r0002-fixed_routed (11) and g3-r0002-fixed_blocked as the primary-backbone equivalent 00 anchor. Its detached bias is trained, unlike a literal zero loss, but never enters inference; exact baseline equality was observed. Existing g3-r0001-mean_only, g3-r0001-dispersion_only and g3-r0001-neither provide learned-head counterparts.

remaining_confounds: M and D are components of one nonlinear objective, so interactions are expected; not additive performance contributions.
Native D can also change under a common logit shift because softplus curvature depends on its mean. The free bias and nonlinear encoder can escape D without contracting all history directions.
Single seed and validation-selected checkpoints; repeated same-seed reference reproduction is not independent statistical repetition.
contrasts.decision_if_supported: If M-only recovers most of the fixed-full loss while D-only approaches the reference, prioritize calibration-induced encoder distortion as a provisional explanation. Compare fixed and learned M/D interactions, and inspect pooled norm and attention entropy without treating diagnostics as causal proof.
contrasts.decision_if_not_supported: If D-only also loses materially, fixed-shape dispersion constraints may be harmful; do not conclude all auxiliary training or all random projections fail. Use centered controls to distinguish bias escape from genuine dispersion constraints.

contrasts.intervention: centered_fixed replaces native expected-label loss by C=mean softplus(c+z-mean(z))-softplus(c), c=logit(clamp(q,0.0001,0.9999)); z excludes redundant output bias, q is detached current nonempty-training-batch label prevalence, and mean(z) is differentiable.
contrasts.control: g3-r0002-fixed_routed is the native fixed-head arm. Cross with centered_learned versus g3-r0002-learned_routed to complete centering x head-shape comparison; include fixed_mean_only and fixed_dispersion_only to interpret which native component causes harm.

remaining_confounds: Centering simultaneously removes the common-logit-shift route and fixes softplus curvature near current-batch prevalence. It is not a matched-gradient-norm comparison; equal aux_weight does not imply equal regularization strength.
A fixed head constrains only its scalar nonlinear projection, not all 16 history directions. The encoder can change ReLU activation regions or move along its null directions.
Current-batch q is noisy and depends on repeated users; no independent-user or calibrated-probability claim. Mean logit c does not imply mean sigmoid equals q.
Fixed versus learned heads match allocated 577 auxiliary parameters, but trainable shape capacity and backward cost differ. Centered output bias is allocated but unused.
512 validation-row diagnostics at selected checkpoint cannot reveal transient training gradients or prove calibration drift caused final quality loss.
contrasts.decision_if_supported: Predeclared directional screen: centered_fixed should recover at least 0.002 AUC versus g3-r0002-fixed_routed and have a smaller pooled-history norm on the identical diagnostic prefix. If the fixed centering effect exceeds the learned centering effect, treat calibration/head-adaptability interaction as preliminary support. Improvement over baseline-din must be separately measured and repeated before selection.
contrasts.decision_if_not_supported: If fixed centered remains poor, reject this implementation as a quality improvement; sustained fixed-shape constraints, strength mismatch or nonlinear escape remain alternatives. If it only matches baseline, report recovery without a new best model. Do not keep this branch merely because centering identities hold.

contrasts.control: Native g3-r0002-learned_routed (same outcome as g3-r0001-expected_permuted) and centered_fixed. Difference of centering effects across head shapes is the interaction of interest.
